concepts.def: Jesus' death by execution on a Roman cross
Jesus rising from the dead on the third day
Jesus' death restoring humans' relationship with God
Being saved from sin and given eternal life
God's free, undeserved love and forgiveness
Jesus returning to heaven 40 days after Easter

walkthroughs.body_html:
Christians believe Jesus was crucified under Pontius Pilate around 30-33 CE.

'For God so loved the world that he gave his one and only Son...' (John 3:16).

On the third day he rose — the resurrection — appearing to Mary Magdalene and the disciples (Luke 24, John 20).

Atonement = Jesus' death makes humans 'at one' with God. 'Christ died for our sins' (1 Corinthians 15:3).

Catholics emphasise grace through faith and works/sacraments. Protestants emphasise 'salvation by grace through faith' alone (Ephesians 2:8-9).

The Ascension (40 days after Easter) marks Jesus' return to heaven.

Christians believe in judgement after death (Matthew 25:31-46 — sheep and goats).

Heaven = eternal life with God; Hell = separation from God.

Catholics also teach Purgatory — a state of purification before heaven for those who die in grace but need cleansing.
